endangerment.comment: Salvadoran Sign Language (7117-esn) = Vulnerable (60 percent certain, based on the evidence available) (LESSA is in use in families with generational deafness, in public deaf education, within deaf associations, at churches with interpreted services, for distributing information on the internet, and for official interpretation for the government of El Salvador. The growth and spread of deaf education using LESSA suggests that the percentage of LESSA users will increase. Multigenerational deaf families all use LESSA (Ciupek-Reed 2012).) [Lewis et al. 2016](cldf:lewis:paul:etal:ed:16)

classification.sub: Not lexically close to other sign languages in the America (**hh:v:Parks:Sign-Language-Comparisons**):82 and consequently judged to be an isolate (**hh:h:Fox-Tree:Sign-Central-America**), also by **hh:hv:Wittmann:Classification-Signees(**):283 on opaque grounds.
